new_rows.claim: **Wherever unconditional (Benson 1976) life sits on the goban, the stored WZO2 table certifies a single score (L==H).** No entry containing a Benson-alive chain for either colour falls in ANY bracketed class (L<H), and in particular none straddles zero: Z-and-either-alive = 0 over all 49,428 entries at 3x3 and all 99,133,036 at 4x4, over the fresh-start slices (24,330 / 48,505,262), and position-level 0 of the 624 (3x3) / 507,484 (4x4) positions holding a straddling entry. Converse slice: 0 of the 895,216 pin_0 draw-by-loop entries at 4x4 (and 0 of 1,248 at 3x3) contain a Benson-alive chain for either colour. **SCOPE:** a measured property of the stored tables, not a derived theorem; the L<H columns are the ko-sensitive region still distrusted pending Track A, but the finding's force is categorical (alive entries never co-occur with a non-T bracket) so it survives value distrust unless regeneration changes which entries are L<H. **INDEPENDENTLY CONFIRMED at 3x3** by claude-opus-5/orcha during T393 adjudication: a separate implementation (textbook Benson written from the definition in Python, WZO2 layout from src/artifact2.zig, colex decode from src/colex.zig, calling neither src/t393_census.zig nor rules.benson_alive) reproduced all 13 published 3x3 figures exactly. 4x4 not re-derived; carried by the bracket partition matching the committed A4 pin census on all four counts, by the join being sound by construction (anyB/anyW computed per position and consumed in one loop reporting 2,766,492 in the T cell and 0 in Z, so a defect zeroing Z would have to be bracket-selective), and by the headline predicate either=anyB-or-anyW being independent of decodeKeyByte. **CAVEAT (T398):** the doc's argument for why this is non-trivial is FALSE and withdrawn — Benson life bounds the owner's AREA, not the score; 90 entries at 3x3 hold a Black alive chain at value <= 0, 60 exactly 0, lowest L==H==-2 with a two-stone chain. The correction makes the result LESS forced, not more.

**Coexisting unconditional life — both colours simultaneously holding a Benson-alive chain — begins at 4x3.** Counts with denominators: 0/57 (2x2), 0/489 (3x2), 0/12,675 (3x3), **2/321,689 (4x3, a colour-inverse pair)**, **324/24,318,165 (4x4, 0.0013%, one in ~75,000)**. Completes the T382 zero-alive series, whose 4x4 row was pending: a colour at zero Benson-alive stones in 99.9987% of 4x4 legal positions. **SCOPE:** 3x3/4x4 from WZO2; 4x3 from the WZO1 artifact (no WZO2 exists at 4x3) — WZO1-denominated and labelled as such; legality and Benson aliveness are rule-family-independent position predicates, cross-checked by the 4x4 count being identically 324 on the WZO1 checkpoint and the WZO2 table. 3x3 row independently confirmed (0/12,675) by claude-opus-5/orcha.

**Unconditional life at 3x3 exists WITHOUT a stone at the centre point — the operator's shape claim is refuted.** 206 of the 1,766 3x3 positions where a colour is Benson-alive have the alive colour holding no centre stone (182 with the centre completely empty, 24 with the opponent's stone there); **38** distinct shapes modulo rotation/reflection, **19** modulo rotation/reflection/colour-inversion (exactly 2:1, consistent with zero two-life positions at 3x3). The diamond `.x./x.x/.x.` (cells 1,3,5,7 — the four edge midpoints; the brief's two named shapes are the same cell set) is Benson-alive with an empty centre. **INDEPENDENTLY CONFIRMED** by claude-opus-5/orcha: 1,766 / 206 / 182 / 24 / 38 / 19 and the diamond's aliveness all reproduced from a separate Benson implementation. This is the operator's loss and it cuts toward 'territory does not require the centre at 3x3'.
